# useOptimisticAction

Shows a change the moment it is made, undoes it and says why if the server refuses it, and tells the page what is still pending. `base` is the server's state, which the app fetches and stores; a change stays applied over it until its `commit` settles, so update `base` before `commit` resolves. A refused change is taken out and the rest stay, so a slow commit never blocks the next press, and quick changes to one item settle in the order they were made. `commit` is a plain function that returns a promise, so any data layer fits.

```tsx
import { useOptimisticAction } from "@/registry/ouro/lib/ouro/use-optimistic-action";
```

## Example

```tsx
const { value, pending, reason, run } = useOptimisticAction(liked);
<Button pressed={value} data-ouro-pending={pending ? "" : undefined} onClick={() => run((on) => !on, () => api.like(id))}>Like</Button>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `ReactionBar`'s `optimistic` prop instead when the change is a reaction.
- Use React's `useOptimistic` instead when the app needs no reason and no pending state to read.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | `T` |  |
| `options` | `OptimisticActionOptions` | `{}` |

## Returns

`OptimisticAction<T>`

## Types

### `OptimisticAction`

What `useOptimisticAction` returns.

```ts
interface OptimisticAction<T> {
  /** The state to draw: `base` with the changes that are still waiting for their answers applied, oldest first. */
  value: T;
  /** Whether any change is waiting for its answer. */
  pending: boolean;
  /** Why the latest refused change was undone, in words for the person; `undefined` until one is refused, and again after the next change. */
  reason: string | undefined;
  /**
   * Shows `apply` at once and runs `commit`; resolves `true` when `commit` settles, or `false` when it
   * rejects, after the change is undone and `reason` is set. Never rejects.
   */
  run: (apply: (current: T) => T, commit: () => Promise<unknown>) => Promise<boolean>;
}
```

### `OptimisticActionOptions`

Options for `useOptimisticAction`.

```ts
interface OptimisticActionOptions {
  /** Turns a refusal into the words the person reads. @default the error's `message`, else "That didn't go through" */
  describe?: ((error: unknown) => string) | undefined;
}
```
